newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan opposition party hails Bhutto's removal.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan opposition party hails Bhutto's removal.

text.p: Pakistan's main opposition party welcomed President Farooq Leghari's overnight dismissal of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's three-year-old government on Tuesday. Sartaj Aziz, secretary general of the Pakistan Muslim League (PML), also praised the president's action in appointing veteran politician Meraj Khalid, 80, as caretaker prime minister to supervise elections set for February 3, 1997.
"We welcome the decision and welcome the appointment of Meraj Khalid," Aziz told Reuters by telephone, describing Khalid as a "neutral, patriotic person".
He said the prospect that elections would be held in 90 days' time augured well for democracy and the political process.
Aziz urged the caretaker government to set up a system to bring people involved in corruption to justice and not wait for elections. "It should be a bi-partisan and credible system," he said.
Bhutto's government had been taking Pakistan downhill and had failed to win the trust of the business sector, he said.
Aziz said the PML leadership would meet later on Tuesday in Islamabad to discuss its future strategy for the elections.
PML leader Nawaz Sharif was prime minister for 30 months from 1990 to 1993 when his government was abruptly dismissed by then president Ghulam Ishaq Khan.
He was reinstated by the Supreme Court briefly, but then resigned to make way for a caretaker government that supervised the October 1993 elections that brought Bhutto to power.
